title: Chinese NAND Maker YMTC Reportedly Expects Memory Shortage to Last Another Three Years
source_used: eTeknix (relaying TechPowerUp, which cites The Wire China)
key_facts: eTeknix (6 Oct 2026), thanking TechPowerUp, reports that China's YMTC, a NAND flash memory maker, expects the global memory shortage to last at least three more years.
The claim is attributed to The Wire China: 'According to The Wire China, China's YMTC expects this NAND shortage to last another three years.'
eTeknix says YMTC has already started raising the prices of its memory chips, which will push up the prices of final devices.
YMTC is the world's fourth-largest NAND maker with a market share of around 14%, focused on the consumer market rather than data centres.
In recent months YMTC has been shifting toward the more profitable data-centre chip market, which eTeknix says is one reason the shortage lasts longer.
eTeknix says Micron has already said the shortage would last a long time and that the figures match other forecasts.
An analyst's post on X dated 5 Oct 2026 (Jukan) is embedded in the article, repeating that even YMTC thinks the boom will run three more years.
XenoSpectrum's headline (6 Oct 2026, text not readable) says 'YMTC Employee Says Memory Shortage Could Last 3 More Years', so the attribution may be to one employee rather than the company.
quote_evidence: According to The Wire China, China's YMTC expects this NAND shortage to last another three years.
YMTC is the world’s fourth-largest NAND memory manufacturer, with a market share of around 14% and a clear focus on the consumer market rather than professional or data center sectors.
In fact, the company itself has already started raising the prices of its memory chips, which will cause the prices of final devices to increase accordingly.
why_it_matters_hint: A long memory shortage keeps prices of memory-based products high for device buyers.
event_date: Reported 4 to 5 Oct 2026 (The Wire China, then TechPowerUp on 5 Oct 2026)
notes: TechPowerUp (HTTP 403) and The Wire China (Cloudflare block) could not be opened; TweakTown and XenoSpectrum also sit behind a Cloudflare check. Text read at eTeknix, which credits TechPowerUp and The Wire China; the link to the specific Wire China article was not found. Attribution unclear: XenoSpectrum's headline says an employee, eTeknix says the company. Second-hand, single original source. The gloss 'NAND flash, the type used in phones and storage drives' in the entry is general knowledge, not from the article.
